results.title: Today’s front pages: Friday, November 13, 2026
results.content: Myjoyonline.com brings you the front pages of the various newspapers across the country.

results.title: “It was a dry field” – Somalia Captain complains about Sekondi Stadium pitch
results.content: Somalia captain Abdulsamed Abdullahi has raised concerns about the state of the pitch at the Sekondi Sports Stadium, following his sides 2-0 loss to Ghana. Speaking after Thursday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON 2027) Qualifier, Abdullahi said “To be honest, it was a dry field. A little bit hard to get good pace on […]

results.title: We can be more intense – Interim Black Stars coach
results.content: Interim Ghana coach Kim Lars Björkegren has said the team needs to be more intense when they face Somalia again on Monday. The Black Stars secured a 2-0 win over Somalia in a Group C Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) 2027 Qualifier, at the Sekondi Sports Stadium on Thursday. While the result; Ghana’s first win […]

results.title: Ghana steps up campaign for ITU Council, Radio Regulations Board seats
results.content: Ghana has stepped up diplomatic engagements to secure positions on two key governing and regulatory bodies of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), holding talks with six countries at the ongoing ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, Qatar.

results.title: Permanent Black Stars job is not a question for me – Interim coach
results.content: Black Stars interim coach Kim Lars Björkegren says securing the permanent Ghana coaching position is not his immediate concern, insisting his responsibility is to help the team win matches and qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

results.title: 100% local processing of cocoa beans achievable but requires political will – Dr Opoku Gakpo
results.content: Agricultural analyst Dr Joseph Opoku Gakpo says the government’s plan to ensure 100 per cent of Ghana’s raw cocoa beans are processed locally by 2030 is achievable, provided it has strong political will.

results.title: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 opens today at Ghud Park, Accra Mall
results.content: The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 opens today at the GHUD Park, Accra Mall, bringing together businesses and consumers for a three-day exhibition of Ghanaian products and services.

results.title: UN welcomes Kofi Annan’s appearance on new GH¢100 banknote
results.content: The United Nations in Ghana has welcomed the decision to feature former UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan on the Bank of Ghana’s newly introduced GH¢100 banknote, describing it as recognition of his enduring contribution to global peace and diplomacy.

results.title: Owabi treatment plant shutdown disrupts water supply to parts of Ashanti Region
results.content: Residents in several communities in the Ashanti Region are expected to experience water supply interruptions after Ghana Water Limited (GWL) temporarily shut down the Owabi Water Treatment Plant following heavy rainfall.

results.title: Mahama pledges dialogue to resolve UTAG-GTEC dispute
results.content: President John Mahama says the government is prepared to engage the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG) and the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to resolve disagreements over the regulation of tertiary institutions.

results.title: US$200m chicken import bill puts local poultry production in focus – Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has questioned Ghana’s annual spending of about US$200 million on chicken imports, arguing that local maize and soybean production could support a stronger domestic poultry industry.

results.title: Gov’t plans 3% discount on GoldBod’s gold purchases after taking over programme costs from BoG
results.content: The government plans to introduce a 3% discount on small-scale gold purchases in 2027 to reduce the cost of accumulating foreign exchange and building reserves through domestic gold purchases.

results.title: Peasant agriculture cannot solve Ghana’s food problems – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana must move beyond peasant agriculture and modernise food production to reduce its dependence on imports.

results.title: Kofi Arko Nokoe joins MCE to oversee second PWD support disbursement in Nzema East
results.content: The Member of Parliament for Evalue-Ajomoro-Gwira, Kofi Arko Nokoe, has joined the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Nzema East,Kuah Dickson, to oversee the disbursement of support to Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) in the municipality.

results.title: 2027 Budget: Promised 24-hour economy incentives still missing
results.content: The 2027 Budget does not specify several incentives proposed to attract businesses into Ghana’s 24-hour economy programme; instead, it outlines a narrower set of tax measures for participating enterprises.

results.title: Samira Bawumia champions solar-powered healthcare, clean cooking at COP31
results.content: Former Second Lady of Ghana, Hajia Samira Bawumia, has called for increased investment in solar-powered healthcare systems and clean cooking solutions, highlighting their importance in protecting women and children from the health effects of climate change.

results.title: Ghana urges inclusive AI development as One Million Coders registrations exceed 140,000
results.content: Ghana has called for artificial intelligence (AI), satellite connectivity and other emerging technologies to be designed around people's needs, warning that technological advancement must not deepen existing inequalities or leave underserved communities behind.

results.title: ‘It cannot continue’ – Ato Forson challenges Ghana’s $3.5bn food import bill
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has called for a shift towards modern commercial agriculture to reduce Ghana’s annual US$3.5 billion food import bill.

results.title: ‘Do you want me to crash the country?’ – Ato Forson asks critics demanding huge spending
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has defended the government’s expenditure record, saying a substantial part of available public funds is going towards settling inherited debts and restoring confidence in the economy rather than financing new spending.

results.title: IJM Ghana donates mattresses, appliances to support human trafficking survivors
results.content: The International Justice Mission (IJM) Ghana has donated mattresses and household appliances to the Human Trafficking Female Adult Shelter operated under the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection to improve living conditions for survivors receiving care at the facility.

results.title: NDPC reviews national monitoring and evaluation manual to strengthen development planning
results.content: The National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) has begun a stakeholder review of the second edition of Ghana’s National Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Manual to improve its effectiveness and application across public institutions.

results.title: African Political Parties Initiative announces inaugural leadership, with Asiedu Nketiah as chair
results.content: Ghana’s National Democratic Congress (NDC) National Chairman, Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has been named the inaugural Chair of the African Political Parties Initiative (APPI), placing him at the head of a continental platform seeking to strengthen political party institutions and cooperation across Africa. The African Governance Centre (AGC), which established the initiative, announced the composition of APPI’s inaugural Bureau Leadership following the Second African Political Parties Summit (APPS 2026), held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from November 5 to 7. Mr Asiedu Nketiah was endorsed as Chair on November 7, following his nomination by an interim committee and approval by participating political parties at the summit. The Bureau will serve an initial three-year term. The Bureau is supported by ten Regional Vice-Chairs representing political parties across Africa’s five regions.

results.title: Mahama discusses lecturers’ welfare, university funding with UTAG
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has engaged the leadership of the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG) on a range of concerns, including lecturers’ welfare, recruitment challenges, research funding and tensions with the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC).

results.title: ‘Come and buy our cocoa beans, but add value here in Ghana’ – Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has urged international cocoa buyers to process beans in Ghana, as the government pursues plans to increase local processing to 50% by 2028 and 100% by 2030.

results.title: Ghana-Canada trade rises 56% to $752m in 2025 – Deputy Trade Minister
results.content: Ghana and Canada are seeking to expand trade and investment ties, with bilateral trade between the two countries reaching US$752 million in 2025, up 56 per cent from US$483 million recorded in 2024.

results.title: Looming crisis as 1.34 million young Ghanaians out of work, school and training – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has warned of a looming youth employment crisis, saying 1.34 million young Ghanaians are neither working, studying nor receiving training.

results.title: Ato Forson credits ‘shock therapy’ for Ghana’s two-year stabilisation
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has credited an aggressive fiscal adjustment programme with stabilising Ghana’s economy in two years, saying the government deliberately exceeded its primary surplus target to rebuild policy credibility.

results.title: US doctor kills building manager after long-running dispute over mould, police say
results.content: A doctor who had been in an ongoing dispute over mould and other issues at his Washington DC apartment fatally shot his building's manager and fired at four others before killing himself, police say.

results.title: We saved more; now we must tackle jobs – Ato Forson defends 2027 shift
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson defended the government’s shift to job creation in 2027, arguing that stronger-than-required fiscal savings have created room to tackle youth unemployment.

results.title: Taking back 1% of GDP in 2027 won’t harm economy – Ato Forson
results.content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson defended plans to take back 1% of GDP in fiscal savings in 2027, arguing the government exceeded its earlier primary surplus target to restore economic stability.
